components.css: .ds-secondary {display:inline-flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;gap:7px;border-radius:6px;font:600 11px/1.6 "Segoe UI",system-ui,sans-serif;min-height:35px;padding:8px 12px;cursor:pointer;transition:background .16s,color .16s;background:var(--hover,#272727);border:1px solid var(--border-strong,#7a7a7a);color:var(--text,#ededed);} .ds-secondary:hover:not(:disabled) {background:var(--hover,#272727);} .ds-secondary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent,#d4d4d4); outline-offset: 4px; } .ds-secondary:disabled {opacity:.48;cursor:not-allowed;} @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { * {animation:none!important;transition:none!important;} }

narrative.overview:
The user-selected dark workspace uses restrained light grey accents to keep reading, editing, and diagnostic feedback central. Black grounds and charcoal surfaces make a compact, familiar tool environment. System UI type is intentional for this code workspace; monospaced code and mathematical notation retain their own functional voices.

The source is the implemented global stylesheet and workspace, shell, learning, experiment, and retrieval-project components. This record captures shipped choices rather than introducing a new identity. Dense controls serve the work, while larger reading regions retain generous line height. Motion is limited to control feedback, expanding results, and running state.
keyCharacteristics: Black and charcoal surfaces with light grey actions and selections, plus distinct semantic feedback colors.
Compact controls, readable prose, and real monospaced code.
Flat bordered panels with feedback adjacent to the editor.
Connected reading, experiment, and project surfaces with responsive navigation and a mobile description/code switch.

rules.name: The Explicit State Rule
rules.body: Pair semantic colors with icons and wording: green success, red failure, amber caution, and blue information. Keep ordinary actions and working surfaces neutral.

rules.name: The Separate Reading Roles Rule
rules.body: Use UI type for explanations and controls, monospace for code and filenames, and serif notation only for mathematics.

rules.name: The Flat Workbench Rule
rules.body: Separate adjacent working regions with tone and borders; retain the existing flat surface treatment.

dos: **Do** retain dark charcoal working surfaces and light grey interaction emphasis with explicitly labelled diagnostic states.
**Do** preserve distinct UI, code, and mathematics type roles.
**Do** keep keyboard focus visible and pair result color with explicit status text.
**Do** adapt navigation and workspace panels to the available width.
donts: **Don't** turn restrained accents into large bright decorative panels.
**Don't** replace the flat workbench with shadow-heavy floating cards.
**Don't** encode success or failure through color alone.
**Don't** apply dense toolbar typography to long instructional paragraphs.
